trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: To represent the vibrations that make sound, scientists use sound wave diagrams. Waves that are close together represent high-pitched sounds. Waves that are spread out represent low-pitched sounds.

atoms.a: Do you think the wave in this image is representing a high-pitched or low-pitched sound?
Do you think the wave in this new image is representing a high-pitched or low-pitched sound?

instruction.text: Sort each sound wave diagram into high-pitched or low-pitched.

trainers.hint:
The waves of high-pitched sounds are close together.
The waves of low-pitched sounds are more spread out.

feedback.finish: The closer together the waves are, the higher the frequency of the sound. Frequency is a measure of how many waves are produced each second.

instruction.text: Match the sounds these objects make to the frequency of the sound waves that they produce.

trainers.hint: The closer together the waves are, the higher the pitch.

feedback.finish: That’s right! High-pitched noises produce short, close-together sound waves and low-pitched noises make long, spread out sound waves.

instruction.text: Match the sounds these objects make to the frequency of the sound waves that they produce.

finish.text: Well done! The higher the pitch of the sound, the higher the frequency of its waves.

instruction.text: Put the sound wave diagrams into order of pitch, starting with the highest-pitched at the top.
